name: Nellivananathar Temple, Tirunellikka
deity: Shiva as Nellivananathar (Amlavaneswarar, lord of the gooseberry forest), with the goddess Mangalanayaki (Amlakeswari)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirunellikka, near Tiruvarur, honours Shiva as Nellivananathar — lord of the gooseberry (nelli) forest — with the goddess Mangalanayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, its legend tells of celestial trees cursed by Durvasa to be born as nelli trees here, among which Shiva stayed as a self-manifest lingam to honour the sacred gooseberry.

sections.history: Tirunellikka lies about 17 km from Tiruvarur (some 23 km from Mannargudi) in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, counted as the shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The lord here is Nellivananathar, 'lord of the gooseberry forest,' and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Nellivananathar — in Sanskrit Amlavaneswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Mangalanayaki, also called Amlakeswari, in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the nelli (amla, the Indian gooseberry), the fruit dear to Shiva, and the sacred tanks are the Brahma and Surya theerthams.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that trees of the Devaloka were cursed by the sage Durvasa to be born on earth as nelli (gooseberry) trees, and here they stood as a grove; honouring the sacred nelli, Shiva remained among them as a swayambhu, self-manifest, lingam. By tradition Durvasa, famed for his anger, also worshipped here and was blessed to overcome his wrath. So the shrine joins the humble, healing gooseberry to the grace that calms even the fiercest temper.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Tiruvarur include Tirunellikka among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirunellikka the pilgrim comes to a gooseberry-forest shrine where the self-manifest lord honours the humble, healing fruit. Before Nellivananathar and Mangalanayaki, amid the memory of celestial trees and the calming of Durvasa's anger, the visitor finds the quiet, restoring grace of a Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirunellikka is about 17 km from Tiruvarur and 23 km from Mannargudi, in Tiruvarur district (PIN 610205). Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
